fx_rates.quote_convention: units of the listed currency per 1 US dollar (USD base); a fall means the local currency strengthened against the USD
fx_rates.method: Current rates carry the source's own timestamp or ratedate. Period changes and volatility are computed from the dated series stored here. Nothing is interpolated or estimated; an unreachable source is recorded absent with a reason.

matrix_provenance.producer: live backend /api/fx -> fx_api.build_matrix, written into this file by refresh_live_data.py
matrix_provenance.source: the backend FX quote feed (Yahoo Finance): USDKES=X, USDNGN=X, USDZAR=X, USDEGP=X, EURUSD=X, GBPUSD=X
matrix_provenance.as_of_basis: the refresh run that captured it; the /api/fx payload carries no timestamp of its own, so the matrix is stamped with the run time of the companion fx_rates block
matrix_provenance.note: The matrix is a cross-rate snapshot triangulated through USD. The fx_rates block below is a separate producer (fetch_fx_rates.py) and every figure in it carries the source's own timestamp. Where the two differ for the same pair, the matrix cell is the earlier undated snapshot and fx_rates is the timestamped quote; the matrix is not refreshed to the second.
